confirmed.description: Keshavrao's two wrist manacles are about a full arm span apart, with no chain between them. One cuff is at the barrel on the far right and the other is in Nagoji's grip. That breaks the short wrist chain, about a forearm long, that the chapter fixes for both men. Keshavrao wears that chain in 1.2, 2.3, 4.5, 8.2, 9.2 and 9.3.
confirmed.evidence: Page-03 at 1838x2775: Keshavrao's left-wrist cuff is at about (1405,1330), against the barrel, and his right-wrist cuff at about (840,1395), under Nagoji's bandaged grip. No links join them; his arms are spread almost straight out.

verdict.reason: I'm confirming this one. On page 3, panel 3, Keshavrao's arms are spread nearly straight out. His left-wrist cuff (screen right) is on the barrel at about (1405,1330) in the 1838x2775 render, and no chain hangs from it. His right-wrist cuff (screen left) is at about (840,1395), just below where Nagoji's bandaged hand grips his forearm. No chain runs between the two cuffs. The only chain at his right cuff goes left to Nagoji's left-wrist cuff and collar chain, so the links are muddled there too. Nagoji's own raised right cuff, the one gripping, has no clear chain to his other wrist. The chapter does not allow this. Script 1.1 fixes the irons for the whole chapter as wrist manacles joined by a short slack chain about a forearm long. CONTINUITY.md row 3 and the script's continuity note say the same. Script 3.3 also needs Nagoji's own wrist chain to swing and clang against Keshavrao's cuffs. With a forearm-long chain, Keshavrao could not hold an arm-span pose, and the short chain matters later in the plot (6.4, 7.1, and 9.3, where it catches on the rope). The missing chain is easy to see at print size. The panel runs the full page width, the cuffs are drawn large, and the wide pose is the whole action of the panel, set right under the line "Do not let the chain drag you." This is a costume and prop continuity error confined to one panel, so it is major, not a blocker.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's raised right wrist is bandaged but has no iron manacle, and no wrist chain runs to his other hand. Script and bible both say every iron stays on until he goes into the sea. He has the manacle in 5.5 before this and in 6.3 after it.
confirmed.evidence: Page-06 at about (300-345, 470-545): the bandage wraps the wrist below the hand gripping the chain ring, and no cuff is drawn. The only iron near his other hand is a loose shackle at about (440,640) on the broken beam.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 6, panel 1. Nagoji's raised right hand, which grips the pen-chain ring, has a bandage around the wrist but no iron manacle. In the original, the wrist sits at about (330-400, 470-560). His other hand rests on the broken beam at about (440-540, 580-680). It grips a loose bit of shackle that is not on his wrist, and that hand has no bandage either. The tunic and the "Quickly." balloon hide that wrist, and no wrist chain runs between his hands anywhere in the panel. The script and bible do not allow this. Script 5.5 says "wrists still manacled," and its continuity note says "every iron stays on into the sea." The bible's chapter 3 row lists the wrist manacles joined by a short chain, plus bandaged hands and wrists. The art itself breaks the rule: Keshavrao in the same panel has a cuff on each wrist, and Nagoji's cuffs are back in 6.3 right after. The raised wrist is a large, well-lit shape in a full-width panel, so readers will see it at print size. It is a localized costume and continuity error, not a wrong identity or a missing beat, so major is the right severity.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's hinged iron collar, empty since 5.5, is missing as he climbs the ladder. His neck is bare apart from a thin dark cord line at the nape. The empty collar is clearly drawn in 6.1, 6.2, 7.1, 7.2 and 7.4.
confirmed.evidence: Page-06 at about (640-700, 2100-2160): between chin and shoulder there is no thick iron band and no side ring. Keshavrao's collar and ring are clearly drawn in the same panel at about (590,2215).

verdict.reason: I confirm the problem. I zoomed into page 6, panel 4 (original pixels about 630-730 x 2090-2170, at 4x and 8x). Nagoji's head is turned back over his shoulder, so the side and back of his neck are in plain view between his jaw and his trapezius. That stretch is bare wet skin. The only mark on it is a thin dark gold line like a cord. There is no thick hinged iron band and no side ring. The script does not allow this. Line 159 (panel 5.5) says each man "keeps his own empty iron collar". The continuity note (line 336) says "After 5.5 the collar is empty, but every iron stays on into the sea". Panels 6.1, 7.4, 8.1 and 10.1-10.3 also call for it. Elsewhere the art follows that: the collar is heavy and prominent on Nagoji in 6.2, directly above, and on Keshavrao in the foreground of this same panel. His manacles and hobble chain are drawn correctly in 6.4, so only the collar is missing. The figure is small at print size, about 6 mm for the head. Even so, the missing collar shows next to Keshavrao's clear one, and the caption at the top of the same page, "slack iron at the throat", makes the collar a featured prop. This is a localized costume and continuity error, so major is the right severity, not blocker.

confirmed.description: The chapter's two opening captions read backwards. The second caption, "It was the change in the way the ship moved.", sits at the far left where the eye enters the page. The first caption, "The first warning was not the shout...", sits at the top right. Read left-first, "It" has no antecedent. Both boxes are also jammed flush against the panel border, while Ch1 r6 insets its captions.
confirmed.evidence: page-01.png, top panel. The left caption runs x150-700, y515-610 and touches the left border at x148. The right caption runs x1095-1688, y390-520 and touches the right border.

verdict.reason: The placement is real, but "backwards" overstates it, and I rate it minor, not major. I measured page-01.png at 300 DPI. Caption 1, "The first warning was not the shout of a sailor or the crack of thunder.", sits at x1097-1683, y393-520, against the top right of panel 1.1. Caption 2, "It was the change in the way the ship moved.", sits at x152-700, y515-603, against the left border. Caption 1 sits entirely above caption 2; the two overlap by only about 5 px vertically, so a strict top-to-bottom reading gets the order right. The step runs down and to the left, though, across a panel about 5.3 in wide, with roughly 400 px of art between the boxes. Caption 2 is a single line at the left edge, right below where the eye enters the panel and next to Nagoji's head. Many readers will take it first, and then "It" has no antecedent in the chapter's opening line. Ch1 r6 page 1 avoids this by putting its two opening captions level, first one on the left. Swapping the two texts or moving caption 1 to the left is a trivial fix, so this is reading-order polish, not a clearly wrong panel. The flush-to-border point is not a defect. Flush caption boxes are a standard style, nothing in the bible or script forbids them, and this chapter uses them consistently (the 1.2 caption also sits flush on the bottom border).

confirmed.description: Panel edges are ragged and no row fills the column. Left and right edges step in and out from row to row, and the gutter between 6.4 and 6.5 is wider than the others, so the page reads as loosely pasted frames rather than a grid.
confirmed.evidence: page-06.png. 6.1 and 6.2 span x205-1632. 6.3 spans x239-1597. 6.4 spans x148-915 and 6.5 spans x950-1660 (a 35 px gutter against about 5 px elsewhere). Column standard: x148-1688.

verdict.reason:
I measured page-06.png and the claim holds. The page breaks the chapter's grid.

**Panel extents I measured:**
- 6.1: x205-1633, y358-791
- 6.2: x206-1632, y797-1598
- 6.3: x239-1598, y1604-2023
- 6.4: x148-916, y2029-2542
- 6.5: x950-1661

**How that compares with the rest of the chapter:** pages 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 all fill a flush x148-1688 column with gutters of about 5 px.

**What is wrong on page 6:**
- **Left edge:** it moves by 57, 33 and 91 px from row to row. At 300 DPI that is 4.8, 2.8 and 7.7 mm.
- **Right edge:** it sits 56, 57, 91 and 28 px inside the column.
- **Bottom row:** 6.4 sticks out past every row above it on the left. 6.5 stops at a different right edge from every other row.
- **Gutters:** the gap between 6.4 and 6.5 is 34 px (about 2.9 mm). Every other gutter on the page is 5-6 px (about 0.5 mm).

**Visible at print size:** I set pages 5, 6 and 7 side by side as thumbnails. Even at that size, page 6 stands out as stepped and loosely pasted next to the tight grids on 5 and 7. It also faces the clean page 20 in the spread.

**Not allowed by the plan:** the script's page 6 notes, the layout notes (which only cover the insets on 8.3 and 9.1) and the bible say nothing that allows a ragged or inset grid. It is a fitting artefact. Where LAYOUT.json asked for a split second row, LAYOUT-fitted-s7.json moved the split to row 4, and the panels were scaled to their aspect ratio instead of cropped to fill the column.

**Severity:** the art does not need redrawing. Re-fitting or cropping the panels to the standard column with 5 px gutters fixes it. It is still clearly wrong for a whole published page and goes beyond polish, so I am confirming it as major, not blocker.

confirmed.description: The layout is ragged. 8.2 is shrunk to a narrow centred strip, and 8.3 and 8.4 are each inset by a different amount, so no right or left edge lines up below 8.1. The gutter between 8.1 and 8.2 is also wider than the rest.
confirmed.evidence: page-08.png. 8.1 spans x148-1688, y365-1008. 8.2 spans x461-1376, starting at y1021 (13 px gutter). 8.3 spans x167-1670. 8.4 spans x187-1650.

verdict.reason: I measured the borders on page-08.png and the claim holds. The cream background starts at pixel (50,50). Each row's non-background extent gives these panel boxes: 8.1 at x148-1688 (y365-1008), 8.2 at x461-1376 (y1021-1435), 8.3 at x167-1670 (y1440-2098) and 8.4 at x187-1650 (y2103-2542). Gutters are 13 px between 8.1 and 8.2 and 5 px between the others. On most pages in the chapter (1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10) every panel row sits flush at x148-1688. Page 3 also uses centred panels, but their edges match each other (315-1521). On page 8 nothing below 8.1 lines up. 8.3 is pulled in 19 px (about 1.6 mm at 300 DPI) on each side and 8.4 is pulled in about 39 px (about 3.3 mm). A crop of the right edge shows a clear three-step staircase at 1688, 1670 and 1650. That is visible at print size, and it looks like an accident, not a design choice. The script also calls 8.3 "full width". The cause looks like LAYOUT-fitted-s7.json: it sets row heights only (157.1, 98.7, 157.1, 104.6), so each image seems to have been shrunk to fit its row's height, which leaves different side margins. 8.2's narrow centred strip (915 px, about 59% of 8.1's width) could pass as a deliberate hatch inset, and the 13 px vs 5 px gutter difference (about 0.7 mm) is barely visible, so those two points alone would not count. The staircase on 8.3 and 8.4 is real, so I confirm the finding. I rate it minor, not major. The art, lettering, speaker tails and story beats are all fine and nothing is hidden. Fixing it means re-running the page layout so 8.3 and 8.4 sit flush at 148-1688, which may need slight crops, plus centring 8.2 deliberately or widening it. No panel needs redrawing.

confirmed.description: The two insets along the bottom edge (Keshavrao's hands on the hatch rim, and the spar) have no keyline or gutter. They butt straight onto the deck image and onto each other, so they read as a collage seam rather than framed insets. The 9.1 inset, by contrast, has a border.
confirmed.evidence: page-08.png, about y1895-2095. Zoomed, there is no border line between the main image and the inset strip, or between the two insets at about x920.

verdict.reason: The problem is real, but I'd rate it minor, not major. On page 8, panel 8.3, the inset strip (original pixels about y1900 to 2100) has no keyline above it or between the two insets. At the seam between the insets (x about 919), pixel values jump straight from the dark hatch wood (about 15 to 25) to bright surf (about 200 or more), with no dark rule. Along the top of the strip, the only solid black line is the 4px border of the "Wait to free him" caption box. Past the caption (x 1000 and x 1400), no continuous black rule runs across. The inset on page 9, panel 9.1 does have a thin black keyline, so the two pages are inconsistent. The cut is visible at full-page view, so it is not too slight to matter. Still, nothing is lost: the strip sits inside the panel's outer border, and the two insets are clearly separate images (warm hatch wood and hands on the left, blue sea and spar on the right). Both beats the script asks for read correctly, and no action or lettering is hidden. Adding a 3 to 4px keyline around and between the insets would fix it, so this is polish rather than a localized error.

confirmed.description: The art contradicts the line it carries. The script has Nagoji's forearms hooked over the timber with his manacled wrists together, taking the strain off his wrists, and the balloon says 'Hook your arms over the wood.' Instead Nagoji hangs from the beam by his hands with his arms straight and his wrists far apart, and the men copying him also grip with their hands. Nobody hooks an arm over the wood.
confirmed.evidence: In the 3.2 crop Nagoji's two bandaged hands grip the top of the beam about 190 px apart (bandaged wrist at top left, the other hand near x=660). The two men on the right hang by their fists with their elbows straight.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 3, panel 3.2. I zoomed into the panel at 2x. Nagoji's arms are raised and his fists wrap the top edge of the beam. His bandaged left hand is at the upper left and his right hand is about 185 px to the right in the original 1838 px render. His forearms hang below the timber. They are not draped over it, and his wrists are not together. The young man next to him and the turbaned man behind him are posed the same way: elbows bent, fists gripping the top of the beam, forearms below the wood. The old man at the far right is mostly hidden. Nobody in the panel hooks a forearm over the beam.

The script (3.2) asks for "both forearms hooked over the timber above his head, his manacled wrists together over the wood", with the men nearest him copying that grip. The balloon in the same panel says "Hook your arms over the wood." So the art contradicts the line it carries.

This is not too slight to matter. The gripping hands are the main subject of the panel and read clearly at print size, right next to the balloon giving a different instruction. Nothing in the bible or script allows the swap. The bible's forearm-long wrist chain does not excuse it, because the script asks for the wrists together on the wood.

"Hold to the beams!" still matches, and the beat of Nagoji taking command with men copying him comes through, so it is not a blocker. It is a localized staging error that contradicts the dialogue, which is major. The fix is to redraw this one panel with forearms over the beam and wrists together, or to change the line to fit the hand grip.

refuted.description: In this panel Keshavrao no longer matches his Chapter 2 lock and drifts toward Nagoji's type. He has a thick, dark, full moustache instead of a faint youthful one. His curly hair grows long at the nape instead of being hacked short above the ears. His shoulders and forearms are as heavy and muscled as Nagoji's. The result reads as a man in his mid to late twenties, not the narrow-shouldered nineteen-year-old on 07-keshavrao-v15c.png. On page 5 he looks right in panel 2 and on the rest of the chapter, which makes the drift stand out.
refuted.reason: I cropped and zoomed page 5, panel 4 and compared it with Keshavrao in 4.2, 4.5, 5.5, 6.1 and 6.2 and with 07-keshavrao-v15c.png. The art shows only a slight drift, nothing near major. (1) He cannot be mistaken for Nagoji. He wears the grey-brown tunic, has no ear stud, is placed on the right as the script asks, and has a smooth, beardless young face. His moustache is a short brush with no handlebar. Nagoji, beside him, has the ochre tunic, the earring, the long curly mane and the big handlebar. (2) The build complaint does not single out this panel. Keshavrao has the same sinewy, defined arms in 5.5, 6.1 and 6.2, and the approved sheet also gives him visibly muscled arms. In 5.4 his arms and shoulders are clearly smaller than Nagoji's in the foreground; they only look comparable because both men are hauling at full strain. (3) The moustache is a little denser than the 'faint' one on the sheet. But the 6.2 version is about as dark, so it sits within the chapter's normal variation. The curl at the nape is a few tufts behind the ear, not a mullet. His head is only about 150 px tall on a 1838 px page, so at print size these differences barely show. (4) The report also says he 'looks right in panel 2', but the cast overrides have no Keshavrao in 5.2, which weakens the comparison it is built on. At most this is optional polish: thin the moustache and trim the nape curls. It does not break his identity lock.

refuted.description: Pseudo-text is painted into the art. The carved stern castle behind Nagoji has two gilt cartouches filled with glyphs that look like letters (roughly 'SDAI' / '8DAI'). The standing rule bans text of any kind in the art. The fix is local: paint the cartouches out or turn them into plain scrollwork. No redraw is needed.
refuted.reason: I checked page-08.png, panel 8.1 at 1:1, 4x and 8x. The two gilt cartouches on the stern castle are where the reviewer said (left about x 1215-1275, y 505-540; right about x 1455-1505, y 535-570). Each is about 50 px wide, roughly 4 mm by 2.5 mm in print. At 8x they look like interlaced gilt knotwork: closed loops and crossing strands with no consistent baseline or letter spacing. They read as letters only through pareidolia at high zoom. At 1:1 and at half size they look like carved gilt panels, which is ordinary decoration for the carved stern castle the script asks for in 8.1. Nothing in them reads as a word, they are low contrast on dark wood, and they sit in the background behind Nagoji's head. The bible's "no text of any kind" rule is about lettering, signs and inscriptions, and this ornament is too ambiguous and too small at print size to break it. I'm uncertain, so I refute. If anyone still objects, it is minor polish at most (soften the loops into plain scrollwork), not a major problem.

refuted.description: There is a rope that reads as a noose in the hold behind the ladder. One line comes down from above into a wrapped knot on the post, and a long open loop hangs below it. It sits right beside the guard who is about to fall to his death. This breaks the no-nooses rule. Fix it by redrawing it as a flat coil hung on a pin, or by removing it.
refuted.reason: I cropped and zoomed page-07.png, panel 7.1 (about x 780-960, y 760-1180), and also viewed it at roughly print scale. The rope is real, but it does not read as a hanging noose. The turns at the top run horizontally around the wooden post, which is how a rope lashing looks. A hangman's coil would be a stack of turns around a free standing line. Below the turns the loop lies flat against the post. It does not hang open: it closes in a second knot or lashing at the bottom, and a slack tail continues down from there. A noose loop has no knot at its foot, so this breaks the silhouette. The whole reads as a rope belayed or stowed on a hold stanchion, which is a normal ship prop. At print size the loop is only about 0.4 in tall. It sits in a dark background area behind the action, and in the reduced views it reads as a coil hung on a post. The guard falling near it does not make it a noose: nothing in the panel puts a loop near a neck or suggests a hanging, and the guard's death is shown by his fall in 7.2 and 7.3. CONTINUITY.md bans ropes "tied as hanging nooses", and this rope is not tied that way. Since the noose reading is doubtful at best and too slight to matter at print size, I refute it. At most it is optional polish: tidying the rope into a flat coil on a pin would remove any doubt, but it is not a rules violation that needs a redraw.

refuted.description: A chain runs from an overhead hook straight down to a prisoner's neck. The pen chain drops steeply (about 70 degrees, close to vertical) from the ring in the splintered beam to the collar of the bald prisoner on the far right, and it is still taut. The chapter's no-noose staging says no chain hangs vertical above a head and nothing pulls upward on a neck. The script also says the chain sags into the water once the ring tears. Lower the chain's angle or let it go slack into the water so it no longer reads as a tether from overhead to the throat.
refuted.reason: Refuted as a no-noose violation. In page-05.png, panel 5.2, the chain does run from the torn ring (bottom of ring at about x 1532, y 462 original px) to the side ring at the nape of the bald man's collar (about x 1627, y 667). That is about 65 degrees from horizontal, or roughly 25 degrees off vertical. The ring sits well to the left of his head (head at about x 1640 to 1690), so the chain is not vertical and it does not hang above his head. It comes in from up-left to the back of the collar. That matches the rig the script fixes for the whole chapter in 1.1: "at the end of the pen rises at a slant to an iron ring bolted into the beam overhead, off to one side". It is also the same geometry the script asks for in 5.1 ("rises to it at a slant ... does not hang straight down") and that 5.4 needs and shows (the ring hanging at the far end of the chain, with the chain rising to it at a similar steep slant). The bald man is hunched forward, pulling with his hands, and is cut by the panel edge. His collar tilt follows his bent head; nothing shows him being lifted or yanked by the neck. The panel is about 2.5 inches wide at print size, so the chain is a small element in the upper right and reads as a pen chain to a beam ring, not a tether from overhead to the throat. One residual deviation: the 5.2 script says the chain's end "drops and the whole length sags into the water" once the ring tears. The art keeps the chain fairly straight up to the half-torn ring. The script's own 5.4 still has the chain running up to the ring on its last bolt, so this is at most minor polish (let the overhead run droop a little), not a major or a redraw.

refuted.description: Wrong speaker tail. Nagoji's second balloon, "You have seen the dungeon... Tell me which death you prefer.", sits over Keshavrao's back in the foreground. Its tail rises toward Keshavrao's jaw and collar, not toward Nagoji, so the line reads as Keshavrao's. The balloon is also squeezed into a narrow seven-line column.
refuted.reason: I checked this at full resolution and the art does not show the problem. The tail of the "You have seen the dungeon..." balloon starts on the top edge of the balloon at about x320-357, y955 and rises up and to the right to a tip at about (417,892). If you extend that line, it runs straight through Nagoji's face at about (650,700). It angles away from Keshavrao's head, which is above and to the left of the tip. Keshavrao is seen from behind and his mouth is not visible. A tail aimed at his jaw would rise straight up or lean left, and this one does neither. The tip is actually closer to Nagoji's chained fist (about 30 px) than to Keshavrao's jaw (about 80 px). Putting the speaker's balloon over the listener's back is a standard over-the-shoulder layout. The text also settles who is speaking: Keshavrao answers the question in 4.2 ("With you, I prefer the one that involves a chance"), and the script gives both 4.1 lines to Nagoji. At print size the tail clearly reads as rising toward Nagoji. The seven-line balloon is an evenly broken oval and is fully legible. A longer tail would be a small polish at most, not a wrong-speaker error.

refuted.description: The reading order breaks the exchange. Keshavrao's second line, "And if there is no such thing?", is lettered higher on the page than Nagoji's off-panel answer, "Towards air. Towards anything that floats." Readers get question, question, answer: "Move where?", then "And if there is no such thing?", then "Towards air...".
refuted.reason:
I measured the three balloons on a crop of page-03.png, panel 3.5 (y in 300 DPI pixels). "Move where?" runs from y2092 to y2202, centred at about x690. "Towards air. Towards anything that floats." runs from y2233 to y2408 at x385 to x870. It sits directly under the first balloon and starts below its bottom edge. "And if there is no such thing?" runs from y2165 to y2342 at x1240 to x1505, on the far side of Keshavrao's head.

The reviewer's top coordinates are correct. The right balloon's top is about 68 px (about 5.8 mm) higher than the left balloon's top. But the two lower balloons overlap vertically for about 109 px, roughly 62% of their height. "And if" overlaps "Move where?" by only about 37 px. Its centre (y2253) is 67 px from the "Towards air" centre (y2320) and 106 px from the "Move where?" centre (y2147). So "And if" reads in the same row as "Towards air", not as "Move where?", and within that row the left balloon comes first.

"Towards air" also continues a left-hand column directly below "Move where?". The "Move where?" tail points down and inward, away from the right balloon. The order the script needs (Move where? / Towards air / And if) is therefore the natural reading order.

The stagger is small, and a reader would at worst pause for a moment, because the line "no such thing" only makes sense after "anything that floats". This is not a broken exchange at print size. As optional polish, the right balloon could drop 70 to 100 px so its top sits level with or below the "Towards air" top, which would remove any doubt.

refuted.description: The reading order is ambiguous between the two lower balloons. Nagoji's "If we stay, we may drown before they can load." is on the left and almost level with Keshavrao's "If we take it, they will shoot us." on the right. Read left-first, Nagoji's rebuttal comes before the objection it answers.
refuted.reason: I measured page-06.png at full resolution, and the art does not show the problem. Keshavrao's balloon (right) runs from about y1097 to y1217, and Nagoji's balloon (left) from about y1178 to y1352, so the reviewer's numbers are correct. But the only overlap is the white padding at the bottom of Keshavrao's balloon. His single line of text sits at y1141-1171, completely above the top border of Nagoji's balloon (y1178). It also sits about 58 px (about 5 mm at print size) above Nagoji's first line of text (y1229-1293). Nothing is lettered side by side, so the usual rule (the higher balloon reads first) gives the script's order without a tie for left-first to break. The placement helps too: Keshavrao's balloon sits right under the right-hand end of "The hatch. We need air. We need to see.", where the eye stops, and the drop down-left to Nagoji's balloon is the normal Z path. Read at normal page size, the order is the script's: hatch, then "If we take it, they will shoot us.", then "If we stay, we may drown before they can load." The words also guide the reader, since "before they can load" only makes sense after "they will shoot us". The script puts Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, so this stagger is the standard fix for that layout. Lifting Keshavrao's balloon a little higher would be optional polish, not a real ambiguity, and certainly not a major problem.

refuted.description: The page does not hold the art column. Four of the five panels (3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.5) are letterboxed about 167 px in on each side, and only 3.4 runs full width. This leaves a ragged stack with wide cream margins, unlike the full-width rows of the Ch1 r6 standard. Ch1 insets at most one panel, by about 30 px.
refuted.reason: The measurements are right, but the comparison behind them is wrong, and the layout falls within what the house standard already accepts. On page-03.png, panels 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 3.5 span x312-1520 and 3.4 spans x148-1688, which matches the report. The claim that "Ch1 insets at most one panel, by about 30 px" is false, though. In chapters/ch01/renders/r6, page 6 has three inset rows at three different widths (x204-1628, x412-1420 and x260-1572, so 56, 264 and 112 px in from each side), stacked between two full-width rows. That stack is more ragged than ch03 page 3. Ch1 r6 pages 7 and 8 each have two inset rows (80 to 92 px), and Ch2 r1 pages 3 and 5 inset four or five rows by up to 236 px. The pipeline README (fit-layout and --keep sections) treats side bars as the designed fallback: when faces, keep zones or painted regions stop a frame from being cropped to the column, the crop is "left taller (side bars) rather than cutting any of them". The script does not require column width for 3.2, 3.3 or 3.5. It describes 3.1 only as "Wide", and the full-width list in the print notes is about resolution, not layout. On page 3 itself, the four inset panels share one width and are centred, with even 6 px gutters, and nothing is cropped. The wave, both arm hooks, the forearm clamp, the two-shot and Keshavrao's close-up all read in full. Balloons and tails sit inside their panels. This is a stepped stack that the Ch1 standard already uses, not a defect that blocks publication.

refuted.description: Nagoji's key line 'You have seen the dungeon. That is what awaits us at the end of this journey. Tell me which death you prefer.' looks like it belongs to Keshavrao. The balloon sits over Keshavrao's foreground shoulder and back, and its tail ends just beside his neck and jaw, about 200 px short of Nagoji's face. The page then reads as Keshavrao putting the question and answering it himself in 4.2.
refuted.reason: I measured the tail at full resolution and the art does not support the misattribution. In page-04.png the big balloon's tail runs from a base at about (340,958) to a tip at about (402,906), so it slants up and to the right. Extending that line lands right on Nagoji's mouth and moustache, at about (590-625, 750). I checked this by drawing the extended line over a crop of panel 4.1. The tip sits in open background, about 85 px right of Keshavrao's collar ring. It points away from Keshavrao. His face is turned away from us and his hidden mouth is above and to the left of the tip, the opposite way from the tail. A short tail aimed straight at the speaker is standard lettering, and it does not have to touch him. Putting a seven-line balloon over the foreground character's back is also normal in an over-the-shoulder shot: the right half of the panel is taken up by Nagoji and his first balloon, so there is nowhere else for it to go. Nagoji's other balloon in the panel, 'Then we die here in the dark.', has its tail on his collar, which already marks him as the speaker in this panel. The dialogue flow confirms it. Keshavrao asks 'And if there is no such thing?' at the end of page 3, Nagoji asks 'Tell me which death you prefer', and Keshavrao answers in 4.2. At print size (about 6.1 in wide) the tail's angle toward Nagoji is easy to see. A slightly longer tail would be optional polish, but there is no real problem here.

minors.description: Keshavrao is drawn at the same height and breadth as Nagoji: broad muscled shoulders, heavy arms, chest hair, the same stance and the same scale. The script wants the contrast of a clearly younger, smaller and thinner man. A milder version of the same heavy build appears on 6.1, 8.2 and 9.1, but 5.5, where both men stand full length side by side, is where the lost size difference shows most.
minors.evidence: In page-05.png panel 5 (y2030-2545), both men stand full length in mirrored poses. In the zoom at x1250-1690, y2030-2300, Keshavrao has broad deltoids and visible chest hair, and his shoulder width is about the same as Nagoji's on the left.

minors.description: Keshavrao's moustache is a heavy, dark, solid bar. It should be the faint wisp of a young man, as on his sheet and in 1.2 and 2.3 of this chapter. With it he looks older here than in the panels before and after.
minors.evidence: Zoom of page-02.png at x840-960, y650-780: the figure in the grey-brown tunic beside Nagoji has a thick black moustache as dense as Nagoji's. On the same page in 2.3 (x920-1690, y1530-2160) his moustache is the correct faint line.

minors.description: Nagoji's ear stud is drawn as a tiny pale silver or white pin instead of the small gold stud he wears on his sheet and in every other panel of the chapter.
minors.evidence: Zoom of page-07.png at x680-1020, y1890-2150: the earlobe shows a pinpoint white or silver dot. Compare the clearly gold stud in 6.2, 8.1, 9.2, 10.2 and 10.3.

minors.description: The background prisoner who says "We will drown down here" has long curly black hair, a moustache and a small gold ear stud. The gold stud is Nagoji's signature. His full beard keeps him apart from Nagoji, but an extra in a two-shot of Nagoji should not carry the stud, so that no one in the hold reads as a double. Remove the earring.
minors.evidence: Zoom of page-04.png at x1180-1450, y2140-2380: the bearded middle prisoner between Nagoji and Keshavrao has a gold stud in his visible earlobe.

minors.description: The background prisoners are drawn bare-chested in loincloths. The script dresses them in grey, brown and off-white rags, and they wear rag tunics in 1.1, 2.1, 4.3 and 5.2.
minors.evidence: Page-03, the whole panel (315-1525, 360-785): the men in the pens on both sides of the flooded aisle are bare-backed with only a wrapped loincloth.

minors.description: The musket and the ladder both change between 2.1 and 2.4 on the same page. In 2.1 the musket has a large brass butt plate and brass fittings, matching 6.3. In 2.4 it has a thin iron butt plate, iron barrel bands and a different double-cock lock. The steep, narrow companion ladder under the hatch in 2.1 becomes a broad open staircase rising to open sky in 2.4. The script says to plant this musket hard because it pays off on page 6.
minors.evidence: 2.1 butt plate (brass) at about (290-500, 1170-1460); 2.4 butt and lock (iron) at about (165-700, 2240-2480); 2.1 ladder at about (1300-1560, 360-1000); 2.4 staircase at about (1440-1680, 2200-2420).

minors.description: The ladder changes construction within the page. In 6.2 it has flat plank rungs between squared stiles, the same as in 7.1 and 7.2. In 6.4 it has round pole rungs lashed with rope.
minors.evidence: 6.2 ladder at about (215-420, 800-1350); 6.4 rope-lashed pole ladder at about (700-900, 2050-2500).

minors.description: The crew at the left wear dark waistcoats, and one wears a black cocked hat, which reads as pirate-film costume. The script dresses the crew in loose shirts and slops with knitted caps or head cloths, and no uniforms. The same crew in 8.1 on this page wear only shirts and head cloths.
minors.evidence: Page-08: the cocked hat is at about (485,1630), and the dark waistcoats are at about (265-515, 1640-1760) and (700-760, 1700-1760).

minors.description: The knee pinning the coil is wrapped in ochre tunic cloth with a hole torn through it. In 9.4, one panel earlier, the knees on the coil are in the cream dhoti.
minors.evidence: 9.5 knee in ochre at about (450-650, 2315-2495); 9.4 knees in cream dhoti at about (300-450, 1925-2055) and (690-760, 2050-2160).

minors.description: Nagoji's feet are planted about a metre apart in a wide lunge, and Keshavrao's are nearly as wide. That is more than the short hobble chain allows. Nagoji's chain runs out of sight behind the dhoti instead of joining his two cuffs.
minors.evidence: Page-05: Nagoji's ankle cuffs are at about (380,2450) and (695,2515), with the chain from the left cuff disappearing at about (530,2435). Keshavrao's cuffs are at about (1280,2505) and (1470,2495).

minors.description: In every panel of the chapter the collar ring sits at the front of the throat, with a chain hanging down the chest. The bible row for chapter 3 and script 1.1 put the ring at the side. It is drawn the same way everywhere, so only the bible spec is broken.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's collar ring is at about (745,615) on page 1, with a chain dropping to his wrists. Front rings appear the same way at page-03 (835,1735), page-09 (685,1935) and page-10 (695,1700).

minors.description: The barnacles on the underside of the spar look like a cluster of small skulls: round grey shells with two dark 'eye' holes and an open 'mouth'. In the chapter's final drowning image this adds macabre imagery the script did not ask for. Soften them into ordinary conical or acorn barnacles. The same skull-like shells show more faintly on the spar in 10.3.
minors.evidence: page-10.png, 10.5, upper right, on the spar above Nagoji. About x 1390-1690, y 2030-2145 (original px). Similar shells in 10.3 at about x 1250-1595, y 1565-1670.

minors.description: The balloon order is weak. The first line, "Storms break ships...", is at the top right above Keshavrao's head. The second, "The men above will think...", is larger and sits at the left by Nagoji's mouth, so it pulls the eye first. The right balloon is also jammed against the top border, and the left balloon's tail touches Nagoji's moustache.
minors.evidence: page-03.png, fourth panel. The right balloon starts at y1482 against a panel top of y1477. The left balloon starts at y1595 at x150.

minors.description: The same backward-Z placement as 1.1. The first balloon, "Quiet down there...", is at the right. The longer second balloon, "If any of you break your chains...", sits lower left against the panel border and draws the eye first. It also leaves a one-word widow, "over."
minors.evidence: page-01.png, fourth panel. The right balloon top is at about y1770. The left balloon top is at about y1845, at x150, flush with the border.

minors.description: Keshavrao, on the right, speaks first, but Nagoji's reply is lettered at the left. The stagger, with the right balloon higher, mostly carries the order, but a left-first reader gets Nagoji's echo of "If the ship breaks" before Keshavrao says it.
minors.evidence: page-02.png, middle-right panel. The Keshavrao balloon top is at about y1800 (right). The Nagoji balloon top is at about y1930 (left).

minors.description: "Others." (Keshavrao) and "Quickly." (Nagoji) overlap in height. "Quickly." is on the left, so it can be read before the line it answers.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, top panel. 'Others.' spans about y455-570 at x850-1015. 'Quickly.' spans about y530-650 at x480-660.

minors.description: The tail of "And if there is no such thing?" lands on Keshavrao's eye. The tail of "Move where?" points at the empty wall left of his head rather than at him.
minors.evidence: page-03.png, bottom panel. One tail tip is at about (1170,2345), on his eye. The 'Move where?' tail tip is at about (875,2220), on the wall.

minors.description: Nagoji's head is cropped by the top border at the brow, so the beat of him rounding on the prisoners with his teeth bared is jammed against the frame line.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, third panel (y869-1247). His eyes sit about 20 px below the top border, and his forehead and hair are cut off.

minors.description: The "One, two..." balloon overlaps Nagoji's jaw, neck and collar, and its tail sits on his cheek.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, fourth panel. The balloon spans about x615-815, y1545-1665, just under Nagoji's chin at about x560-680.

minors.description: The script calls for jagged, overlapping shout balloons for the off-panel sailors. They are lettered as plain smooth ovals that do not overlap, the same as normal speech.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, middle-right panel. 'Reef the sails! Haul, haul!' and 'Tie that down! Move, you son of a dog!' are smooth, separate ovals.

minors.description: The script asks for the first sailor balloon at upper left, before the impact, and the second at lower right, after it. Both are lettered side by side along the bottom, which loses the before-and-after timing.
minors.evidence: page-04.png, bottom-left panel. Both balloons sit at about y2265-2525.

minors.description: The script tags both of Nagoji's lines as spoken in Marathi, but the lettering gives no language cue (no bracket convention or note).
minors.evidence: page-03.png, second panel. 'Hold to the beams!...' and 'Do not let the chain drag you.' are lettered as plain speech. The lower balloon's tail also sits on Nagoji's chin.

minors.description: The script says the caption "For a moment I was nowhere..." sits in the upper-left inset, on Nagoji's fingers in the rope. It is lettered at the top right of the main image beside Keshavrao instead.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, top panel. The caption is at about x1040-1605, y360-490. The inset is at x148-615.

minors.description: The "Tie it! Around your chest! Quick!" balloon sits nearer Keshavrao than Nagoji, and its tail ends at Nagoji's fists on the rope rather than his head, which weakens the attribution.
minors.evidence: page-09.png, second panel. The balloon spans about x800-1240, y1115-1240, close to Keshavrao at about x1220-1400. The tail tip is at about (790,1080), on Nagoji's hands.

minors.description: "Still, weight is weight." is crammed into a narrow three-line box against the right border, and it clips Nagoji's left fingertips.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, third panel. The box spans about x1425-1585, y1840-2010 and overlaps the fingers at about x1400-1480.

minors.description: Panel 2.3 is letterboxed shorter than 2.2, so the tops and bottoms of the two panels in the middle row do not line up.
minors.evidence: page-02.png. The 2.2 frame runs y1518-2170. The 2.3 frame runs y1530-2158, about 12 px in at top and bottom.

minors.description: The guard's two balloons may be read in the wrong order. 'If any of you break your chains...', the second line in the script, is the larger balloon at the left and overlaps the height of 'Quiet down there...', which sits to the right of his head. Read left to right, the threat comes before the order to be quiet.
minors.evidence: On page 1 at display scale, 'Quiet down there' spans about y 1275-1360 at x 600-1000, and 'If any of you...' spans about y 1330-1490 at x 110-555.

minors.description: The two opening captions are split, and the second, 'It was the change in the way the ship moved.', sits at the far left edge where the eye enters the chapter. 'The first warning was not...' is at the top right. A left-to-right reader can take the follow-on line first. The panel is also barely tilted, where the script asks for 'the whole image tilted hard'.
minors.evidence: 'The first warning' box is at about x 790-1215, y 285-375 on the page, and 'It was the change' is at about x 110-505, y 370-435. The horizon of the plank shelves is close to level.

minors.description: The order of the three balloons is ambiguous. Keshavrao's last line, 'And if there is no such thing?' (right), starts higher than Nagoji's off-panel reply, 'Towards air...' (left), and overlaps it in height. A reader following the 'Move where?' tail to the right can read the follow-up question before the answer.
minors.evidence: In the 3.5 crop, 'Move where?' is at y 60-170, 'And if there is no such thing?' at y 135-310 on the right, and 'Towards air. Towards anything that floats.' at y 200-375 on the left.

minors.description: Nagoji's 'Quickly.' sits to the left of Keshavrao's 'Others.' and overlaps it in height, so it is likely read first. That reverses the script, where Keshavrao suggests freeing the others and Nagoji agrees. It costs Keshavrao the initiative.
minors.evidence: In the 6.1 crop, 'Others.' is at about y 105-215 (x 610-810) and 'Quickly.' at about y 175-295 (x 280-460). Nagoji stands left of Keshavrao, so his balloon is the leftmost.

minors.description: The beat of this panel is Nagoji turning on the prisoners with his teeth bared, but his head is pushed against the top border and cut off mid-forehead, so the reaction is squeezed into a sliver at the frame edge.
minors.evidence: In the 5.3 crop, Nagoji's hairline and forehead run off the top edge, and his eyes and bared teeth fall within the top 70 px of a 382 px tall panel.

minors.description: Two script details are lost. First, the narration caption 'For a moment I was nowhere...' should sit in Nagoji's inset (upper left). Instead it is at the top right beside Keshavrao's head, where it reads as describing him. Second, Keshavrao's right hand rests on his thigh rather than twitching at his side for an absent sword. The notes call this the last use of the sword callback planted in Chapter 2.
minors.evidence: The inset (crop x 0-470, y 0-260) holds no lettering, and the caption box is at crop x 890-1460, y 10-135. Keshavrao's right hand is clasped on his knee or thigh at about crop (600,400).

minors.description: Keshavrao looks as if he sits in a small boat on open sea rather than half out of the deck hatch. He holds the rope coiled in his lap and is not trying to pass it round his chest. Both the setting and the action ('fumbling to pass it round his chest') are only weakly told.
minors.evidence: In the 9.3 strip a wooden gunwale-like rim surrounds Keshavrao at waist height, with breaking sea directly behind him. No deck or hatch frame is legible, and both of his manacled hands hold rope loops at his waist.

minors.description: The palms are meant to be reddened and burned so that 10.1's 'The burns on my palms...' pays off. The bandages are stripped, but the palms read as ordinary, unmarked skin.
minors.evidence: In the 9.5 crop both open palms (about x 780-960 and 1030-1180, y 960-1110) are the same tan as the forearms, with no reddening.

minors.description: The script asks for a distant, side-on shot with both men small on the ladder and Nagoji below the guard on the rungs. Here Nagoji is a large figure at the foot of the ladder with one foot in the water, beside the ladder rather than on it. That contradicts 6.4, where he is already several rungs up, and makes the strike a close mid-shot.
minors.evidence: In the 7.1 crop Nagoji's left foot and hobble cuff are in the water at the bottom left (about crop 60-130, 880-970). Only his right foot is on a low rung, and his figure fills about half the panel's height.

minors.description: Keshavrao is supposed to shout into Nagoji's ear with his chin jerked toward the ring. Instead he faces up and to the left, away from both Nagoji and the ring at the upper right, so the reveal of 'Look. The ring.' depends on the reader spotting the ring alone.
minors.evidence: In the 4.5 crop the ring is at about (690,60) in the upper right. Keshavrao's face, at about (430-500, 200-280), tilts up and to the left with his mouth open, and he is not next to Nagoji's ear.

minors.description: The script times the crash with the lettering: the first sailor balloon before impact at upper left, the second after impact at lower right. Both balloons sit side by side along the bottom at the same height, so that timing is lost.
minors.evidence: 'The mainmast!...' is at about y 1610-1735 and 'She is taking water!...' at about y 1580-1745, both in the lower half of the panel at page scale.

minors.description: The beat is lightning freezing the hold 'in one harsh flash, like a portrait'. The panel is lit by warm lamplight with only thin blue lines at the seams, so it reads as an ordinary moment of fear and not a frozen flash.
minors.evidence: The figures in 4.3 are lit warm orange and brown, and the only cold light is thin seam lines across the ceiling.

minors.description: The script asks for jagged, overlapping shout balloons coming from above. These are smooth, rounded, separate balloons, which flattens the panic of the off-panel shouts.
minors.evidence: On page 1, 'Reef the sails! Haul, haul!' and 'Tie that down!...' are smooth ovals with plain upward tails, side by side without overlapping.

minors.description: The script calls for 'the broken ladder' at the empty hatch, but the ladder is drawn intact.
minors.evidence: In the 10.1 crop the ladder in the hatch (about x 1030-1180, y 330-510) has straight rails and complete rungs.
